info.bio:
Las Bangles se formó en Los Angeles, California en 1981, originalmente bajo el nombre de The Supersonic Bangs, que luego se acortó a The Bangs. Sin embargo, un grupo de Nueva Jersey también llamado The Bangs amenazó con demandarlas, por lo que cambiaron su nombre a The Bangles.
La formación original constaba de: Susanna Hoffs (guitarra, voz), Debbi Peterson (batería, voz, bajo), Vicki Peterson (guitarra, voz, bajo)

Esta formación grabó un 45, "Getting out of Hand" b/w "Call on Me".

scenes.name: Música disco
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El funk abre la puerta a la subcultura disco: los gays de Nueva York, perseguidos, crean sus islas sociales en clubes privados y recuperan la despersonalización del éxtasis colectivo. Tres hechos la impulsan: el soul orquestal de Barry White, «Autobahn» de Kraftwerk y el Polymoog. Manu Dibango («Soul Makossa») y MFSB la inventan; Giorgio Moroder casa la música robótica de Kraftwerk con el soul (Donna Summer, «I Feel Love», nacimiento del synth-pop). Van McCoy, el maxi de 12" de Walter Gibbons, Chic, Grace Jones, Gloria Gaynor, Saturday Night Fever, el Warehouse de Frankie Knuckles y el Paradise Garage de Larry Levan. Los reyes del pop: Michael Jackson (Thriller, «el mayor farol de todos los tiempos») y Prince, su contrapartida intelectual.

podcast.title: Only All-Female Rock Band to Score Year-End #1 (1987)
podcast.body: The Bangles are the "only all-female rock band to score a year and hot 100 number one" with "Walk Like an Egyptian," marking a significant milestone in music history. "Incidentally, The Bangles are the only all-female rock band to score a year and hot 100 number one."

podcast.title: Early Booking by Kevin Lyman
podcast.body: The Bangles were among the bands booked by Kevin Lyman, the future founder of the Warped Tour, for university performances at California State Polytechnic University in Pomona when they were starting their career in the early 1980s. "What he would basically do is hire bands like Bad Religion and the Bangles when those groups were just starting out in the book at the university."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transition from Alt-Psych to Pop
podcast.body: The Bangles began as a popular four-piece, all-female band in the US West Coast's Paisley Underground scene around 1982, initially playing alt-psych. They later transitioned into a successful pure pop band, similar to The Go-Go's. "But in the beginning, they were very alt-psych. They were called the bangles."

xref.title: Drummer for The Bangles and Collaborator
xref.body: Debbie Peterson was the drummer for The Bangles, a band that transitioned from the alternative Paisley Underground scene to a hugely successful Top 40 act. After The Bangles' breakup, she went on to play with notable artists like Cindy Lauper, Tom Petty, and Elvis Costello. "Their drummer was Debbie Peterson. Since The Bangles break up, Debbie has played with Cindy Lopper and Tom Petty and Elvis Costello, just to name a few."

xref.title: Influence on Future Female Artists
xref.body: Although they lacked widespread commercial breakthrough, Fanny was "tremendously influential on other young women," inspiring future all-female or female-fronted bands that would achieve greater fame, including The Runaways, Heart, The Go-Go's, and The Bangles. "And although commercial success escaped them through four albums before they broke up in 1975, they were tremendously influential on other young women."
